chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah from Ibn Muskān from al-Ḥalabī, all of them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He was asked about the crescents (of the months), so he said: 'They are the crescents of the months. So when you see the crescent, fast; and when you see it, break your fast.' I said: 'Do you see, if the month is twenty-nine days, should I make up that day?' He said: 'No, unless two just witnesses testify for you. And if they testify that they saw the crescent before that, then make up that day.'

key_terms.اَلْأَهِلَّةِ: Crescents (plural of hilal, referring to the new moon sighting)
key_terms.اَلْهِلاَلَ: The crescent (singular, specifically the moon marking the start/end of a month)

ai.seo_question: How does Shia jurisprudence determine the end of Ramadan and the start of Shawwal based on moon sighting?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the lunar crescent sighting as the definitive marker for entering and exiting fasting months, emphasizing the practical application of the 29 or 30-day cycle. He clarifies that if a month completes as twenty-nine days, the thirtieth day is not automatically observed as a makeup day unless two just witnesses testify to having seen the crescent earlier, thereby validating the shorter month. This hadith underscores the Shia reliance on empirical witness testimony (shahada) for calendar determination, distinguishing it from mere calculation in this specific context of validating the month's length.
